_what_this_is: Grading wave BGL3. The 330 open core units, examined one batch at a time by execution rather than by reading: for each unit an input was built where the quantity it reports genuinely cannot be computed, the unit was run on it, and what came back was recorded verbatim. Every unit was also run on measurable input, because a unit that refuses everything is as wrong as one that answers everything and the two are indistinguishable without it.
_why_this_matters: Each row here carries an observation, not an opinion. Where the grade is PROVEN it names a test and the sabotage that showed the test can fail, because a guard that cannot fail looks identical to one that passed. Every row is audited:false: these grades have not been argued with, and the measured overturn rate on agent-produced grades in this repository is about one in five, so they are claims until an independent check has tried to refute them.

Fixture: two degenerate neighbourhoods that the unit DOES consume (background): (a) a background with no spread at all, as 50 identical rows, a single row, and 40 rows of a different constant; (b) a 300-row background frozen in the one feature the model uses (LogisticRegression whose live coefficient is 5.80 on 'c' against <= 0.06 on the rest). Observed before: (a) attributions [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0], fidelity 0.0, stability 0.0, base_value == prediction == 0.4919 and ZERO warnings, for a model whose own prediction moves from 0.9999997 to 3.2e-07 when the deciding feature flips sign; (b) c = 0.0000 exactly, silently, against c = 0.5508 (the dominant attribution) on a background that varies in c, while the model still moves from 1.000000 to 0.000001 when c flips. Observed after the fix: (a) ValueError 'LimeExplainer COULD NOT MEASURE any attribution for <id>: none of the 4 background column(s) has any spread ... which reads as no feature influenced this decision. Supply a background with at least two distinct rows'; (b) UserWarning '1 of 4 background column(s) have no spread [\'c\'], so LIME never varied them and the 0.0 contribution reported for each was NOT measured' plus params['unperturbable_features'] == ['c'], which reaches the DB row through to_db_row. On measurable input: the varying 300-row background returns c as the largest attribution (0.5508, more than 4x the next feature) with fidelity 0.3516, params['unperturbable_features'] == [] and no warning; the second fixture, keyed on feature 0, returns 0.7167 with fidelity 0.6278; and a background of only TWO distinct rows still answers (0.9847, fidelity 0.9998), so the refusal is aimed at the unmeasurable case and not at scarcity. lime scales its perturbations by each background column's spread, so a column with no spread is never sampled and its weight of exactly 0.0 is the absence of a measurement wearing the strongest all-clear an attribution can give
vfairness.xai.explainers.lime_adapter.Li.sabotage: refusal condition -> `if False and ...`: red. Refusal made unconditional (`if names:`): the healthy control red. params key forced to []: the disclosure pin red. Spread check made blind (`if False:` inside _unperturbable_features): the disclosure pin red. Restored, green.

vfairness.xai.explainers.anchors_adapter.judgement: Batch xai-2. Fixture: a 300-row background (well above MIN_BACKGROUND_ROWS = 30) frozen in 'c', the only feature the model uses; controls: the same model with a varying background, and a constant model with a 200-row varying background. Observed before: rule=[], precision=1.0, coverage=1.0, n_background=300, background_sufficient=True, no background_warning key and no warning of any kind, against rule=['c > 0.72'] with coverage 0.25 for the same model and row on a varying background. Observed after the fix: params['empty_rule_warning'] = 'the anchor search returned the EMPTY rule, so precision 1.0 and coverage 1.0 are those of the whole perturbation space and state no sufficient condition for this decision ... no rule could condition on [\'c\'], which hold a single value in the background', the same text as a UserWarning, and params['unperturbable_features'] == ['c']. On measurable input: the varying background still returns rule=['c > 0.72'] with coverage 0.2459 and 0.2538 on two runs (the KL-LUCB search is stochastic, so the pin asserts a non-empty rule and coverage < 1.0 rather than a value), unperturbable_features [], no empty_rule_warning and no new warning. A background frozen in a feature the model does NOT use still yields rule=['c > 0.72'] and gets the narrower unperturbable note (['a']) instead. A genuinely constant model still receives its empty rule, which is the true explanation of a constant model, and is told so rather than refused. the empty anchor's 1.0 / 1.0 belong to the whole perturbation space and read as a perfect universally applicable explanation; the adapter already disclosed exactly this failure mode below 30 background rows, where it is least likely to matter, and said nothing at 300 rows where the frozen column hid the deciding feature
vfairness.xai.explainers.anchors_adapter.sabotage: `if not rule:` -> `if False:`: disclosure pin red. Same line -> `if True:` (note on every call): the healthy control red. `elif unperturbable:` -> `elif False:`: the found-rule-with-a-frozen-column pin red. Restored, green.

vfairness.xai.explainers.dice_adapter.Di.judgement: Batch xai-2. Fixture: (a) a black box exposing predict_proba only, no .predict and not callable, which DiCE generates from happily while the adapter's own original-prediction call has nothing to use; (b) an all-categorical frame (region, band) with a model keyed on region, so the recourse flips no numeric feature. Observed before: (a) prediction=0.0 on the returned CounterfactualExplanation and 0.0 in to_db_row, with NO warning at all, because _predict_label's 'model exposes neither predict nor __call__' branch returns None silently; base_value=0.0 for a method that computes no reference output. (b) both counterfactuals came back proximity=0.0 and feasibility=1.0, the two best recourse scores there are, for a flip of region alone. Observed after the fix: (a) prediction is nan in the object and in the row, params['prediction_reason'] says 'COULD NOT MEASURE the original prediction ... prediction is NaN, which is not the label 0', and a RuntimeWarning fires on the previously silent branch; base_value is nan with params['base_value_reason'], matching the anchors disposition. (b) proximity and feasibility are both nan with a RuntimeWarning naming the features that changed; the counterfactual itself is still returned. On measurable input: the numeric frame is unchanged: prediction 1.0, first counterfactual proximity 0.312795, feasibility 1.0 as a measured in-range fraction, no prediction_reason key and no COULD NOT BE MEASURED warning. 0.0 is the DECLINED class, the exact label a recourse explanation exists for, so it cannot also mean the model was never asked; and proximity 0.0 (no distance at all) with feasibility 1.0 (every change in-distribution) are the neutral-best pair returned when there was no numeric change to normalise or bound-check
vfairness.xai.explainers.dice_adapter.Di.sabotage: prediction fallback -> 0.0: red. prediction forced to nan always: the healthy control red. proximity/feasibility fallbacks -> 0.0 / 1.0: red. proximity forced to nan always: the healthy control red. Restored, green.

vfairness.xai.storage.audit_artifact.bui.judgement: Batch xai-2. Fixture: the claims in its own docstring, tested against each other: identical content twice; one attribution moved by 1e-06; only an Explanation.timestamp changed; seed None; and an empty evidence set (explanations=[], decomposition=None). Observed before: two calls on identical content agree (fe6c4c970533cfc4...); changing one attribution changes the digest; changing only a timestamp does not; seed None changes it and is carried as None; the empty bundle carries explanations [] and decomposition None beside a real 64-char digest. On measurable input: the populated bundle keeps the timestamp ON the bundle while leaving it out of the digest, and digest_excludes is declared inside the hashed payload so a verifier can reproduce it. nothing here is unmeasurable, the content address covers exactly what it claims and excludes only the declared clock paths, and both absences stay visible and machine-readable rather than being dressed as content
vfairness.xai.storage.audit_artifact.bui.sabotage: _content_explanation made to keep the timestamp (digest covers the clock): red. Empty explanations replaced with a placeholder row: red. Restored, green.

vfairness.xai.worker.runner.WorkerLoop.r.judgement: Batch xai-2. Fixture: a stubbed Supabase client, three ticks each, in two worlds the loop cannot tell apart: a pgmq read that answers with an empty list, and one that raises RuntimeError('relation "pgmq.q_xai_jobs" does not exist') on every call. Observed before: both worlds ended on the same line, 'INFO XAI worker stopped cleanly'. The broken world logged a per-tick WARNING with the traceback, which is real disclosure, but the one summary a supervisor reads contradicted it and neither the loop nor a host program had any way to tell an idle worker from one that never read its queue. Observed after the fix: counters _polls_answered / _polls_failed (0 and 3 in the broken world), the per-tick warning now carries the running count and says 'This is NOT an empty queue', and the exit line becomes 'ERROR XAI worker stopped after 3 failed poll(s) and NOT ONE answered read of queue xai_jobs: it never learned whether there was work, so this is NOT a clean stop'; a partially failing run gets its own WARNING summary. On measurable input: the genuinely empty queue still reports (3, 0) and 'XAI worker stopped cleanly' with no WARNING or ERROR record, so an idle worker is not alarmed about. _pop_one must return None for both an empty queue and a failed read, so 'no work' and 'could not tell whether there is work' collapsed into the clean answer at the exit surface
vfairness.xai.worker.runner.WorkerLoop.r.sabotage: exit branch -> `if False:` (always clean): red. Exit branch -> `if True:` (never clean): the healthy control red. `self._polls_failed += 1` -> `pass`: the poll pin red. Restored, green.
